title.narrative: Green Cities 3 W2 - Ganja Water and Wastewater

description.narrative: The Bank is supporting critical investments in water and wastewater infrastructure in the city of Ganja in several phases (the "Project"). The Borrower is the Republic of Azerbaijan, and the loan is for the benefit of the Azerbaijan State Water Resources Agency (the "ASWRA"), a government entity responsible for managing water resources in Azerbaijan. Phase 1 of the Project, consisting of a sovereign loan of up to EUR 35 million, was signed on 22 January 2025. Phase 2 of the Project, consisting of up to EUR 120 million sovereign loan, will be used to finance the construction of a new wastewater treatment plant ("WWTP") with a capacity of 400,000 population equivalent (P.E.) and the associated infrastructure, as well as the water supply, sanitation and stormwater management network in Ganja. Phases 1 and 2 are part of a broader Priority Investment Programme ("PIP") with an estimated total cost of EUR 410 million, encompassing the holistic rehabilitation of the water and wastewater sector in the Ganja city. The Project will be implemented under the EBRD's Green Cities and aims to address the priority environmental challenge of 'water availability and quality' identified in the Ganja Green City Action Plan ("GCAP"). The Government prioritises the Project considering the acute need for improvement of the deficient urban water and wastewater infrastructure in Ganja. Upon the Project completion, it is expected that part of city of Ganja will benefit from uninterrupted water supply and wastewater sanitation services, while flood risks will be mitigated through the introduction of a stormwater management system.
